assumptions: The admin group endpoints are the ones under api/admin; admin/stats is in the app group but its path is under /admin, so I tagged it
Admin endpoints use auth=users, so $auth.id is the caller
The role check's error_type accessdenied is acceptable for the precondition
org_id on tenants is the filter the customer means, not on users
confusions: The template admin_endpoints_check_role says a function called require_admin is the usual example; the customer wants the admin or support_lead value check, which the policy cannot see, so the role logic lives in the function body only
No documented way to scope a rule to an API group's path prefix; the tag scope was the only option that reached admin/stats
Parse warns that tag admin is on no query until the tag is pushed; it is expected but reads like a real problem
Unclear whether db.edit accepts a where filter; the policy docs show field_name/field_value only
wished_for: A way to scope by path prefix (for example /admin) rather than by tag, so new endpoints under the prefix are picked up without a tag
A recipe for org-level tenancy (filter on org_id) that is separate from owner-based own_records_only
A note on whether db.edit and db.patch accept a where clause for filtered writes
parse_errors_seen: rule warning: tag admin on no query on this branch
rule warning: function require_admin_role not on this branch
why_confidence: The call-first rule is well supported by the template, but it only checks the call, not the role logic, and the admin tag must be applied to each endpoint. TEN-001 covers all tenants reads and writes, but two expected findings (PATCH db.edit and stats count) remain by design. I did not run policy evaluate, so I have not seen the real findings.
